column2: Augustan Textile Colours Ltd. (now Augustan Textile Colours Pvt. Ltd.) v. Director of Industries & Anr.
column3: (2022) 6 SCC 626; 2022 INSC 408; Civil Appeal No. 2830 of 2022
column12: Could a sick unit's tax exemption be withdrawn, or was it protected by promissory estoppel?
column13: Dismissed: single-unit exemption was beyond s 10(1); no PE against statute (paras 27 to 31).
column14: Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. (1979) 2 SCC 409 (para 28)

column2: Chowgule & Company Ltd. v. Assistant Director General of Foreign Trade & Ors.
column12: Could an exporter claim an additional licence under the old export policy after the policy changed?
column13: Dismissed: incentive is policy the Union can change; no PE, no parity claim (paras 5 to 8).
column14: No precedent on promissory estoppel applied by the Court; appellant relied on Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. (1979) 2 SCC 409

column2: Union of India & Ors. v. A.B.P. Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
column3: (2023) 20 SCC 343; 2023 INSC 525; Civil Appeal No. 986 of 2011
column12: Could the Union withdraw a 5% customs duty concession after the importer had opened a letter of credit?
column13: Allowed: amendment valid; no PE against legislative power or vested right in a concession (paras 26 to 29).
column14: Prashanti Medical Services & Research Foundation v. Union of India (2019) 9 SCR 828 (para 26)

column2: State of Gujarat v. Arcelor Mittal Nippon Steel India Ltd.
column11: Entry 255(2), Notification of 05-03-1992 (s 49(2) Gujarat Sales Tax Act 1969)
column12: Was purchase tax payable after the unit passed gas to a power company, despite promissory estoppel?
column13: Allowed: conditions breached; PE cannot alter exemption terms or override statute (paras 19 to 22).
column14: Commissioner of Central Excise, Bangalore-I v. Bal Pharma Ltd. (2011) 2 SCC 620 (para 20.3)

column2: Dr. Prakasan M.P. & Ors. v. State of Kerala & Anr.
column3: (2024) 20 SCC 694; 2023 INSC 772; Civil Appeal No. 7580 of 2012
column12: Could teachers who retired earlier claim the later, higher retirement age on legitimate expectation or estoppel?
column13: Dismissed: retirement age is policy; no vested right, so PE and legitimate expectation fail (paras 11, 17 to 19).
column14: New Okhla Industrial Development Authority v. B.D. Singhal (2021 SCC OnLine SC 466) (paras 12 and 18)

column2: State of Himachal Pradesh v. M/s Kundlas Loh Udyog
column3: 2026 INSC 534; Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 26731 of 2025
column11: Clauses 16(a) and 16(b), Himachal Pradesh Industrial Policy 2019
column12: Could an expanding existing unit claim the concessional power tariff meant for new units?
column13: Allowed: expansion units get only the expansion benefit; PE cannot create an entitlement the policy never gave.
column14: IFGL Refractories Ltd. v. Orissa State Financial Corporation, 2026 INSC 18

column2: IFGL Refractories Ltd. v. Orissa State Financial Corporation
column3: 2026 INSC 18; 2026 SCC OnLine SC 28; Civil Appeal No. 66 of 2026
column11: Clauses 4.1, 5.1 and 11.4.4, Industrial Policy of Orissa 1989
column12: Was IFGL entitled to the sanctioned subsidies for its new plant despite the claimed subsidy limit?
column13: Allowed: the new plant qualified as a new unit; sanctioned subsidies payable with 9% interest.
column14: Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. (1979) 2 SCC 409

column2: Puja Ferro Alloys Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Goa
column11: Goa (Prohibition of Further Payments and Recovery of Rebate Benefits) Act 2002
column12: Could the companies keep the 25% power rebate after the State withdrew it and sought recovery?
column13: Dismissed: claim barred by res judicata; promissory estoppel yields to overriding public interest.
column14: G.R. Ispat Ltd. v. Chief Electrical Engineer, 1999 (1) Goa L.T.

column2: Satish Chander Sharma & Ors. v. State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors.
column11: Article 32, Constitution of India; HP Corporate Sector Employees Pension Scheme 1999
column12: Could retired corporation employees claim pension under the 1999 Scheme after its 2004 withdrawal?
column13: Dismissed: Article 32 cannot reopen a final judgment; no promissory estoppel as PF rights were restored.
column14: State of Himachal Pradesh v. Rajesh Chander Sood (2016) 10 SCC 77

column2: M/s Rewa Tollway Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors.
column11: Proviso (c) to clause (C), Article 33, Schedule 1-A, Indian Stamp Act 1899
column12: Could the State charge higher stamp duty under a 2002 amendment despite an earlier Rs 100 stamp-paper assurance?
column13: Partly allowed: no promissory estoppel against legislative power; public interest overrides executive assurance.
column14: Hero Motocorp Ltd. v. Union of India (2022)

column2: Hero Motocorp Ltd. v. Union of India & Ors.
column12: Could the Union be held to its 2003 promise of 10 years' excise exemption after GST replaced the excise regime?
column13: Dismissed: no promissory estoppel against legislative power; the GST Act ended the exemption.
column14: M. Ramanatha Pillai v. State of Kerala (1973)

column2: State of West Bengal & Ors. v. Gitashree Dutta (Dey)
column12: Could the State cancel declared fair price shop vacancies to implement the Food Security Act?
column13: Allowed: no estoppel against a statute; applicant in an unfinalised selection had no vested right (paras 25 to 29).
column14: A.P. Dairy Development Corpn. Federation v. B. Narasimha Reddy (2011) 9 SCC 286 (para 27)

column2: Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority & Ors. v. Shakuntala Education and Welfare Society & Ors.
column12: Could allottees hold YEIDA to the premium in their leases against a later policy demanding extra payment?
column13: Allowed: no promissory estoppel; policy change in public interest prevails.
column14: Kasinka Trading v. Union of India

column2: State of Maharashtra & Ors. v. Reliance Industries Ltd. & Ors.
column12: Could the State withdraw a captive-power electricity duty exemption despite promissory estoppel and legitimate expectation?
column13: Allowed: power to exempt includes power to withdraw; no vested right; reasonable notice needed.
column14: Shrijee Sales Corporation v. Union of India (1997)

column2: State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. v. Principal Abhay Nandan Inter College & Ors.
column3: (2021) 15 SCC 600; 2021 INSC 551; Civil Appeal No. 865 of 2021
column12: Could the State require aided colleges to outsource Class IV staff, or was it barred by estoppel?
column13: Allowed: aid is not a fundamental right; the State may attach conditions (paras 29 to 30).
column14: T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002) 8 SCC 481

column2: The Vice Chairman & Managing Director, City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd. & Anr. v. Shishir Realty Private Limited & Ors.
column11: Article 14, Constitution of India; Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act 1966
column12: Could CIDCO cancel an allotment and lease deeds without proof of a violation or a pressing public interest?
column13: Dismissed: cancellation unjustified; promissory estoppel can bind the State and yields only to proven public interest.
column14: Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. (1979) 2 SCC 409

column2: Directorate of Film Festivals & Ors. v. Gaurav Ashok Ailani & Ors.
column11: Article 14 of Constitution of India / Administrative Eligibility Regulations
column12: Whether public authorities are estoppel-bound to retain existing criteria for public benefits and awards without modification.
column13: Administrative eligibility criteria can be altered midway for administrative feasibility; no absolute rights exist under promissory estoppel.
column14: State of Jharkhand v. Brahmputra Metallics Ltd. (2020)

column2: State of Punjab & Ors. v. Amrit Vanaspati Co. Ltd.
column11: Punjab General Sales Tax Act / Industrial Tax Concession Notification
column12: Whether tax exemptions promised via executive press notes can bind the State when the formal statutory notification contains explicit limitations.
column13: No promissory estoppel can lie against the State to enforce an executive concession that contradicts or exceeds the boundaries set by the parent statute and formal notification.
column14: Kasinka Trading v. Union of India (1995)
